title: Public job creation hands out job tokens and trusts caller content_hash, allowing audio poisoning
description:
Found by the sub-agent review of PR #67 (auritus-fa4905). Pre-existing; not introduced by that PR.

`POST /jobs` needs only a site key, and site keys are embedded in public pages. In `cdk/lambdas/router/handler.py` `_create_job`:

1. `content_hash = body.get("content_hash") or _content_hash(...)` trusts the caller's hash. An attacker can register the deterministic hash of a real page's text and voice, with **their own text**. The next visitor's `GET /jobs/{hash}` passes the `site_id` check, and a local or Batch worker narrates the attacker's text as that page's audio. No token is needed.
2. The 201 response returns `job_token`. With it the caller can `PUT /jobs/{hash}/claim`, `POST /presign-upload`, upload arbitrary audio, and `PUT /done`. That skips the worker entirely.

## Proposed fix (needs a decision on the embed contract)

- Always compute `content_hash` server-side from `normalize(text) + voice_id + tts_backend`. If the client sends a hash that does not match, either reject with 400 or ignore it and return the server hash. The embed (`embed/src/index.ts`) and the CLI (`cli/src/auritus/api.py` `create_job`) both send one today.
- Stop returning `job_token` from `POST /jobs`. Only the Step Functions input to Batch needs it; the embed never reads it.
- Optionally rotate or clear `job_token` when a job reaches done or failed.
- Gherkin: a site-key caller cannot claim a job, cannot bind a mismatched hash, and gets no token.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Decision (user, 2026-09-26): reject mismatched hashes; one canonical SHA-256 everywhere; migrate existing jobs; drop job_token from POST /jobs. Implemented in #76. The embed was hashing with 32-bit FNV-1a (41 of 61 live jobs), so the embed moves to Web Crypto SHA-256. Migration copy phase applied to the live jobs table: 39 copied, 19 already canonical, 2 in flight, 1 pre-existing collision (61 -> 100 rows). Remaining after merge: release site (promote to main) then cdk deploy, then `remove-legacy --apply`.

Production rollout 2026-10-17 (legacy account AuritusBackend, us-east-1):
- Deployed v1.0.0 (9d0c016) with aws-cdk 2.1141.0. cdk diff beforehand: Lambda code updates (RouterFn, AuthorizerFn, BatchTelemetryFn, CostReconciliationFn) and an OperatorAuthLayer version replacement only; no table, bucket, or Cognito changes. Deploy succeeded in 38s.
- Verified live: POST /jobs with the public demo site key and a mismatched content_hash returns HTTP 400 {"error": "content_hash_mismatch"}.
- migrate_content_hashes.py copy: dry run would copy 72 (already canonical 56, in flight 1, canonical exists 1, no text 0). --apply: copy 72; in flight 1; canonical exists 1; no text 0.
- remove-legacy dry run: would remove 113, kept 2 (the in-flight row and the row whose canonical copy predates migration). Independently checked all 113: each canonical row exists and its migrated_from equals the legacy key (112 done, 1 failed).
- remains: remove-legacy --apply was not run; the agent's permission classifier blocked the delete. Ryan runs it, then this issue closes.

comments.author: home
comments.text: 2026-10-19 pre-flight audit of scripts/migrate_content_hashes.py remove-legacy (read-only code review by a sub-agent; live table state NOT verified, AWS SSO expired). Deletable = no migrated_from, non-empty text, recomputed hash != key, and a row exists at the recomputed key whose migrated_from equals this key (script lines ~120-145). It does NOT compare the copy's attributes, does NOT check the audio object exists in S3, and the delete condition is only attribute_exists(content_hash), so a row changed between check and delete would still be removed. Dry run is the default; --apply is the only gate; no backup, no account/profile guard, no confirmation. Reruns are idempotent; a row vanishing mid-run crashes the script. Recommended before --apply: confirm v1.0.0 checkout; AWS_PROFILE=legacy aws sts get-caller-identity must show 335163751677; take a backup (aws dynamodb create-backup --table-name AuritusBackend-AuritusJobsAF7BE862-1SQ1AUUYO8M0E --backup-name pre-remove-legacy-20261019 --region us-east-1); dry run and expect remove 113, kept 2; spot-check 3-5 legacy audio_key objects with aws s3api head-object; apply; rerun dry run and expect remove 0, kept 2. Owner must run or approve --apply.
